enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . .KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 455 PM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

 - Dry and seasonal temperatures through Thursday, with breezy
   afternoon winds.

 - A strong backdoor cold front is set to arrive Thursday night,
   bringing gusty winds and winter-like temperatures into the
   weekend. High Wind Warning is in effect for far west Texas and
   portions of southern New Mexico. Wind gusts up to 60 mph are 
   possible along mountain west slopes. 

 - Freezing temperatures over area mountains may lead to a light
   wintry mix Saturday morning.

 - Mostly cloudy skies behind the cold front, with scattered rain
   showers Friday and Saturday, favoring west Texas.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 931 AM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

The upper-level low moving across the Four Corners will keep
conditions dry and breezy today through tomorrow afternoon.
Precipitation will be to our east as a trailing front keeps 
moisture out of our area. Winds today will be from the west-
southwest at 10-20 mph, and gusts up to 30 mph in Sierra County
and northern Otero County. Winds will shift to the north overnight
into tomorrow as a high pressure system spills into the northern 
Plains, decreasing wind speeds to 5-15 mph during the day. 
Temperatures today and through tomorrow afternoon will be at or 
around seasonal averages. These pleasant conditions belie a
dramatic change ahead.

A second upper-level low will break off from the predominant low
moving across the Plains as a ridge starts to dig into the trough
in the Pacific Northwest. This new low will bring a potent cold
front from the northeast Thursday evening, bringing strong
northeasterly winds to the region, especially out east. Thursday
evening through Friday morning will be the riskiest period for
winds, as sustained wind speeds from 25 to 35 mph will be felt
across the region (though Las Cruces up to Holloman AFB will be in
a pocket of lighter winds at this time). Wind gusts in the High
Wind Watch zones could reach 60 mph or higher. Many of the zones
in the High Wind Watch will likely be upgraded to a High Wind 
Warning later today, especially for El Paso, Hudspeth, and Otero 
Counties. Other zones like Dona Ana County could see a Wind
Advisory at least. Recent rains should keep blowing dust concerns
low, but it cannot be ruled out due to the breezy wind gusts.

Temperatures on Friday and Saturday will struggle to even reach 
60F on Friday as the cold front plummets temperatures to 20-25 
degrees below average. The Black Range and Sacramento Mountains
could feel more like winter than fall on Friday and are expected
to see their first freeze of the season. As moisture from the
second low pulls in moisture from the south, some high terrain
locales may even see a mix of rain and snow early Saturday morning
if the moisture is advected far enough north. Should any snow fall
in the high terrain, little to no accumulation is expected due to
ground temperatures being too warm. Outside of the high terrain,
some isolated to scattered showers are possible in the morning 
hours on Friday in the eastern reaches of Hudspeth County. Rain 
chances diminish on Saturday and temperatures begin their climb 
back to normal on Sunday as the cutoff low off the Baja coast gets
picked up by an upper-level trough moving north of us. Another 
Pacific low is visible on both the extended GFS and ECMWF runs 
early next week, which could bring an increase in showers and 
storms by midweek next week, though confidence in impacts is 
currently low.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 455 PM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

VFR conditions expected for the valid period. Aside from morning 
FEW060-080, ceilings will be unlimited at all four TAF sites. 
Some low end gusty winds from the west will be present for a few 
hours in the afternoon before dropping off and shifting more
northerly in the late afternoon. 

After 00Z tomorrow, a strong cold front will arrive from the 
northeast tomorrow evening. Winds will shift to the northeast and 
become very strong. Winds will be at least 08030G40KT with higher 
gusts to 50 knots possible. Low level wind shear will also occur 
tomorrow night, especially over KELP. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 931 AM MDT Wed Oct 14 2026

Limited fire weather concerns today and tomorrow. Min RHs today
will be above 20%, and for Thursday, lowland Min RHs will be in
the mid-to-upper teens and up to 30% in the mountains. Low end
gusty winds from the west likely by this afternoon and the north
on Thursday.

A strong backdoor cold front (moving east to west) will move into
the region Thursday night. Winds will shift to the east in the
evening hours and increase drastically. The strongest winds will
be west of the area mountains as well as Otero, Hudspeth, and El
Paso Counties. Sustained wind speeds of 25-35 mph likely for most
of the region, with high-end wind gusts reaching 60 mph in the
mountains. The strong winds will continue into Friday before
diminishing slightly on Saturday. Precipitation chances will be
low on Friday and Saturday, favoring out east in West Texas as
well as the area mountains. The high mountains may even see a
wintry mix early Saturday morning.
